subject: Post-call: Bluestone — SLO prioritization & topology options
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Hughes <claire@bluestonehealth.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@bluestonehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Bluestone — SLO prioritization & topology options

Hi Claire / Arjun — thanks again for the call today. Quick write-up so we all have the same view and clear next steps. Please reply with anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you raised:
- Tail latency spikes during batch reports (p95 reaches ~800ms, p99 worse) impacting user workflows.
- High per-embedding cost for large-scale vector storage and frequent similarity queries.
- Compliance: HIPAA + customer data residency concerns for certain datasets.

Goals (what Bluestone wants to achieve):
- p95 generation latency under 250ms for short text prompts (interactive UI).
- Sustained throughput of ~600 reqs/s for inference tier with 15k tokens/minute aggregate during peak windows.
- Keep PHI on a private network and ensure audit logs + KMS integration.

Key model requirements we noted:
- Mix of low-latency and high-quality variants: deploy smaller int8/quant models for routing-based low-latency paths and larger quantized models for quality-critical batches.
- Streaming support and function/tool calling for structured responses.
- KV cache support to reduce repeated context cost on long session flows.

Topology options discussed (sketch attached):
1) Hosted + Dedicated hybrid (fastest path): start on Redwood hosted API for POC, migrate latency-sensitive endpoints to a Dedicated reserved GPU pool pinned to a model variant optimized for low-latency.
2) Private VPC (longer runway): private control plane + customer VPC with KMS/HSM integration for PHI — recommended if Bluestone needs strict data residency.

Immediate next steps
- Ben to follow up with a capacity model & topology sketch (attached). (Ben: EOD tomorrow)
- We will share SOC2 and network architecture checklist (link below).
- Schedule an ops deep-dive to nail sizing, telemetry, and failover plan — propose Tue 11/24 or Wed 11/25.

Attachments: bluestone_mutual_action_plan.pdf; topology_sketch_v1.drawio.png
Links: SOC2 report (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1SOC2example/view)

Thanks — I captured owner for each ask above.

Appreciate the topology sketch attachment — opened it briefly and it looks like a good start. Ben — can you include performance assumptions for batching and expected token-level cost with and without prefix caching?

Subject: Re: Post-call: Bluestone — SLO prioritization & topology options (technical follow-up)

Claire / Arjun — quick technical follow-up with concrete numbers and a suggested deployment topology. See attached capacity spreadsheet for a worked example.

High-level deployment (recommended POC -> production path):
- Edge ingress: customer API Gateway -> Redwood routing layer. Short interactive prompts route to a low-latency pool (gpt-small-quant-int8) with KV prefix caching enabled. Quality-critical requests routed to a larger quantized model (gpt-70b-quant) in a separate pool.
- Dedicated reserved pool (US-West primary, EU-West failover): pin 4x A100-80GB for the low-latency pool and 2x A100-80GB for the high-quality pool as a starting point. Autoscale burst to an extra 2 GPUs in peak.
- Caching/batching: continuous batching with dynamic latency buckets. Expect batching to lower per-token GPU time by ~18-30% for non-interactive batches. Prefix/KV cache hit rate assumptions: 40–60% on session-heavy flows — this reduces per-token external compute by similar margin.

Latency & throughput estimates (subject to workload profile):
- Low-latency pool (gpt-small-quant-int8)
  - p50 ~ 40–70ms, p95 ~ 180–240ms (with target batch size <= 8 and KV cache hits), p99 ~ 400–650ms (depends on tail queuing).
  - Sustained throughput per A100 (interactive): ~150–220 reqs/s depending on avg tokens/request.
- High-quality pool (gpt-70b-quant)
  - p50 ~ 150–250ms, p95 ~ 400–700ms depending on sequence length and batching.

Telemetry (minimum set to validate SLOs):
- Per-request: request_id, model_variant, tokens_in/out, request_size, user_id (hashed), route_id.
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 generation latency, queue latency, end-to-end request time.
- System: GPU utilization, GPU memory, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, disk I/O for embeddings store.
- Billing/Cost: tokens generated, model variant mapping to cost bucket, monthly committed vs burst usage.

Security/compliance notes:
- For PHI flows we recommend Private VPC with KMS integration. Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and retention/audit log export. On-prem air-gapped installs are possible via our Private on-prem package but require a longer lead time (60–90 days) and additional SOW items.

Attached: capacity_model_estimate.xlsx (worked example showing three commit sizes and expected latency/cost tradeoffs).

Next steps (owner):
- Ben: finalize capacity spreadsheet with Bluestone-provided token profile (Ben, EOD Thu).
- Jasmine: schedule ops deep-dive for 11/24 or 11/25.
- Claire: confirm procurement's preferred commit tiers to include in the pricing sheet.

—

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is super helpful. Procurement has asked me to confirm three committed sizing bands (we'll send exact numbers tomorrow), and they also want a comparison table for Dedicated vs Private (including lead time and minimum commit).

Two quick questions before the ops deep-dive:
1) For the Private on-prem option, can you outline early whether Redwood provides the installer image + support for customers to operate the GPUs themselves, or if Redwood operates the stack under an enterprise managed service? We may need both options documented.
2) For KMS: we require FIPS 140-2 (or FIPS 140-3) compatible KMS and rotation logs accessible to our security team. Can Redwood confirm compatibility?

We can meet Tue 11/24 at 10am PT if that works for the Redwood ops team. Please confirm and include dial-in/meeting link.
